context: Attribute names with labels, levels, role, data source, physical mechanism, and directional dependency hints (known upstream drivers and downstream effects) — structured to support causal discovery without fully specifying the DAG.

variables.name: N07muVerMo
variables.label: 10.7-micron vertical motion
variables.source: GOES infrared 10.7-micron channel
variables.mechanism: Infrared brightness-temperature tendency provides a proxy for mid-tropospheric ascent; rapid cooling indicates rising air parcels.

variables.name: SubjVertMo
variables.label: Subjective vertical motion assessment
variables.source: Forecaster manual synthesis of available data
variables.mechanism: Expert integration of radar, satellite, and sounding data to estimate dominant vertical motion character.

variables.name: QGVertMotion
variables.label: Quasigeostrophic vertical motion
variables.source: 500 hPa height field; QG omega equation
variables.mechanism: QG forcing (vorticity advection + thickness advection) drives synoptic-scale ascent/descent. Strong positive QG omega promotes deep convection initiation.

variables.name: CombVerMo
variables.label: Combined vertical motion
variables.source: Aggregation of N07muVerMo, SubjVertMo, QGVertMotion
variables.mechanism: Consensus vertical-motion signal used as the primary dynamic-lifting input to the forecast cascade.

variables.name: AreaMesoALS
variables.label: Area of meso-alpha-scale lifting
variables.source: Synoptic + mesoscale analysis
variables.mechanism: Spatial extent of organized upward motion at meso-alpha scale (200–2000 km); modulates where convection can be sustained over northeastern Colorado.

variables.name: SatContMoist
variables.label: Satellite moisture contribution
variables.source: GOES water-vapor channel; precipitable-water retrievals
variables.mechanism: Water-vapor radiances diagnose mid-tropospheric moisture; dry intrusions suppressing convection vs. moist plumes enhancing CAPE.

variables.name: RaoContMoist
variables.label: RAO center moisture reading
variables.source: NWS/RAO surface and upper-air moisture analysis
variables.mechanism: Operational moisture analysis integrating surface dewpoints, rawinsondes, and model output; primary ground-truth moisture input.

variables.name: CombMoisture
variables.label: Combined moisture
variables.source: Aggregation of SatContMoist and RaoContMoist
variables.mechanism: Consensus moisture signal; higher combined moisture increases CAPE and severe hail potential.

variables.name: AreaMoDryAir
variables.label: Area of moisture / dry-air intrusion
variables.source: Synoptic moisture analysis
variables.mechanism: Mid-level dry air from the southwest creates potential for high-based convection and large hail; moist mid-levels favor electrification but smaller hail.

variables.name: VISCloudCov
variables.label: Visible-channel cloud cover
variables.source: GOES visible (0.65-micron) satellite
variables.mechanism: Daytime cloud cover from visible imagery; distinguishes cumulus from cirriform cloud and indicates boundary-layer mixing and capping.

variables.name: IRCloudCover
variables.label: Infrared-channel cloud cover
variables.source: GOES IR (10.7-micron) satellite
variables.mechanism: All-hours cloud-top temperature; cold tops indicate deep, vigorous convection while warm tops indicate shallow or stratiform cloud.

variables.name: CombClouds
variables.label: Combined cloud cover
variables.source: Aggregation of VISCloudCov and IRCloudCover
variables.mechanism: Consensus cloud-cover signal used to diagnose BL heating, capping, and insolation available for destabilization.

variables.name: CldShadeOth
variables.label: Non-convective cloud shading
variables.source: Visible satellite; cirrus or mid-level cloud analysis
variables.mechanism: Cirrus or stratiform cloud shading reduces surface insolation and boundary-layer heating, suppressing CAPE build-up independently of active convection.

variables.name: AMInstabMt
variables.label: Morning instability over mountains
variables.source: Morning soundings and surface obs over Front Range foothills
variables.mechanism: Early-day instability over elevated terrain drives orographic initiation; mountain storms often move onto the plains and serve as hail-producing cells.

variables.name: InsInMt
variables.label: Instability over mountains
variables.source: Combined instability diagnosis, Front Range
variables.mechanism: Afternoon instability over the mountains, incorporating orographic heating and moisture; key driver of convective initiation timing.

variables.name: WndHodograph
variables.label: Wind hodograph shape
variables.source: Rawinsonde hodograph analysis
variables.mechanism: Hodograph shape determines storm-relative helicity and storm motion; DCVZFavor indicates a Denver Cyclone / Convergence Zone environment particularly conducive to supercell development and large hail.

variables.name: OutflowFrMt
variables.label: Outflow from mountain storms
variables.source: Surface mesonet; radar fine-line and gust-front analysis
variables.mechanism: Cold-pool outflow from afternoon mountain convection creates surface boundaries on the plains that serve as focal points for new, often severe, convective development.

variables.name: MorningBound
variables.label: Morning boundaries
variables.source: Morning surface analysis; prior-night outflow and frontal remnants
variables.mechanism: Pre-existing boundaries (stalled fronts, prior convective outflows) are critical low-level lifting mechanisms; their persistence into the afternoon strongly modulates convective initiation location.

variables.name: Boundaries
variables.label: Active boundaries
variables.source: Synthesis of OutflowFrMt, MorningBound, and surface analysis
variables.mechanism: Resultant surface convergence zone strength; strong boundaries provide focused lifting to overcome CIN and trigger severe convection.

variables.name: CldShadeConv
variables.label: Convective cloud shading
variables.source: Visible satellite; convective anvil and cumulus shadow analysis
variables.mechanism: Active convective anvils shade surrounding boundary layer, reducing CAPE and inhibiting new cell development in adjacent areas while concentrating storms in unshaded corridors.

variables.name: CompPlFcst
variables.label: Composite plains forecast tendency
variables.source: Synthesis of CapChange and InsChange
variables.mechanism: Joint cap-instability tendency summarizes whether the environment is trending toward or away from severe convective conditions; DecCapIncIns is the favored hail environment.

variables.name: CapChange
variables.label: Capping inversion change
variables.source: EML / lid-strength forecast change over plains
variables.mechanism: Erosion of the Elevated Mixed Layer (EML) capping inversion is necessary for explosive convective initiation; decreasing cap with increasing instability is the classic severe-hail precursor.

variables.name: LoLevMoistAd
variables.label: Low-level moisture advection
variables.source: 850 hPa wind and dewpoint analysis; southerly jet
variables.mechanism: Warm, moist southerly advection at 850 hPa raises boundary-layer theta-e and increases CAPE; negative (cold/dry) advection suppresses instability.

variables.name: InsChange
variables.label: Instability change
variables.source: Forecast change in CAPE and lapse rates
variables.mechanism: Increasing instability (rising CAPE, steepening lapse rates) combined with decreasing cap creates the necessary condition for severe convective outbreak.

variables.name: MountainFcst
variables.label: Mountain region (R1) severe-weather forecast
variables.source: Final probabilistic hail-severity forecast, mountain region
variables.mechanism: Terminal forecast node; SVR indicates high probability of severe hail (≥3/4 inch) over the Front Range. Driven by mountain-specific instability and boundary effects.

variables.name: Date
variables.label: Seasonal date bucket
variables.source: Calendar date; phenological hail-season windows
variables.mechanism: Encodes seasonal climatology of moisture, jet stream position, and synoptic pattern frequency. Peak hail season in northeastern Colorado is mid-June through mid-July.

variables.name: Scenario
variables.label: Synoptic-scale weather scenario
variables.source: Expert-defined synoptic pattern classification (A–K)
variables.mechanism: Root contextual node encoding the dominant large-scale synoptic pattern. Each scenario carries distinct climatological priors for CIN, instability, and moisture that propagate through the network.

variables.name: ScenRelAMCIN
variables.label: Scenario grouping for AM CIN
variables.source: Partitions Scenario for AM CIN relevance
variables.mechanism: Scenarios A–B have characteristically lower/absent morning CIN; scenarios C–K span environments with more variable but generally present morning inhibition.

variables.name: MorningCIN
variables.label: Morning convective inhibition
variables.source: Sunrise rawinsonde or surface CIN estimate
variables.mechanism: Observed morning CIN controls whether the cap can be eroded by afternoon heating. Stifling or TotalInhibit implies convection is unlikely without strong synoptic forcing.

variables.name: AMCINInScen
variables.label: AM CIN relative to scenario baseline
variables.source: Normalizes MorningCIN against scenario climatology
variables.mechanism: Anomaly encoding: MoreThanAve morning CIN relative to scenario baseline suppresses convection even in ostensibly favorable patterns.

variables.name: CapInScen
variables.label: Capping relative to scenario baseline
variables.source: Afternoon cap strength normalized to scenario climatology
variables.mechanism: Anomalously low cap (LessThanAve) within a given scenario allows even modest forcing to trigger severe convection; high cap (MoreThanAve) can suppress despite favorable thermodynamics.

variables.name: ScenRelAMIns
variables.label: Scenario grouping for AM instability
variables.source: Partitions Scenario for morning instability character
variables.mechanism: Six instability regime groups; pattern G (for example) typically features enhanced low-level jet and elevated instability, while ABI scenarios are more benign.

variables.name: LIfr12ZDENSd
variables.label: Lifted index — 12Z Denver sounding
variables.source: 12Z rawinsonde, Denver (KDVN/KDEN)
variables.mechanism: Lifted index is a direct instability measure: LI < −5 (LILt_8 boundary) indicates extreme instability and greatly elevated severe hail probability. Measured before peak heating to represent initial-condition instability.

variables.name: AMDewptCalPl
variables.label: AM dewpoint calculation — plains
variables.source: Morning surface dewpoint network, northeastern Colorado plains
variables.mechanism: High AM dewpoints indicate abundant low-level moisture for CAPE generation; directly controls surface-based theta-e and convective triggering potential.

variables.name: AMInsWliScen
variables.label: AM instability relative to scenario
variables.source: Normalizes morning instability against scenario baseline
variables.mechanism: Anomaly measure: MoreUnstable within scenario context elevates hail forecast; interaction with CapInScen determines whether instability can be realized.

variables.name: InsSclInScen
variables.label: Instability scaling within scenario
variables.source: Final scenario-scaled instability
variables.mechanism: Calibrated instability input to forecast nodes; accounts for scenario-specific thermodynamic baseline before propagating instability signal to regional forecasts.

variables.name: ScenRel34
variables.label: Scenario grouping for regions 2/3/4
variables.source: Partitions Scenario for northeastern Colorado plains sub-regions
variables.mechanism: Geographic sub-regionalization of scenario priors; different scenario groups have distinct spatial hail climatology across the plains sub-regions.

variables.name: LatestCIN
variables.label: Latest convective inhibition estimate
variables.source: Afternoon mesoanalysis or sounding-based CIN update
variables.mechanism: Updated CIN at or near forecast valid time; represents the actual inhibition state that convection must overcome. Stifling/TotalInhibit sharply reduces CurPropConv regardless of instability.

variables.name: LLIW
variables.label: LLIW severe-weather composite index
variables.source: Low-Level Index of Wind shear; composite of shear, moisture, instability
variables.mechanism: Combines low-level wind shear, BL moisture, and thermodynamic instability into a single severe-weather index; Strong LLIW correlates with supercell and large-hail environments.

variables.name: CurPropConv
variables.label: Current propensity to convection
variables.source: Real-time synthesis of LatestCIN, LLIW, boundary-layer thermodynamics
variables.mechanism: Immediate probabilistic assessment of whether convection will initiate and sustain; accounts for cap erosion and forcing in a single composite signal fed to forecast nodes.

variables.name: ScnRelPlFcst
variables.label: Scenario pass-through for plains forecast
variables.source: Direct pass-through of Scenario to plains sub-network
variables.mechanism: Preserves scenario-specific CPT calibration for the plains forecast node independent of instability and moisture sub-networks.

variables.name: PlainsFcst
variables.label: Plains severe-weather forecast
variables.source: Final hail-severity forecast, northeastern Colorado plains
variables.mechanism: Terminal forecast node for plains hail. SVR indicates high probability severe hail over the plains. Integrates instability, cap, moisture, boundaries, and scenario priors.

variables.name: N34StarFcst
variables.label: Regions 2/3/4 severe-weather forecast
variables.source: Final hail-severity forecast, NE Colorado sub-regions 2–4
variables.mechanism: Terminal forecast node for sub-regions 2–4 east of the primary plains corridor; influenced by scenario-regional grouping, boundaries, and propagating convection.

variables.name: R5Fcst
variables.label: Region 5 severe-weather forecast
variables.source: Final hail-severity forecast, eastern plains edge (Region 5)
variables.mechanism: Terminal forecast node for the far-eastern fringe; convective potential diminishes with distance from orographic trigger but can be maintained by strong synoptic forcing or propagating systems.

variables.name: Dewpoints
variables.label: Spatial dewpoint pattern
variables.source: Surface mesonet dewpoint network
variables.mechanism: Spatial gradient of surface dewpoints determines the geography of theta-e ridges, moisture convergence zones, and convective initiation corridors.

variables.name: LowLLapse
variables.label: Low-level lapse rate
variables.source: Surface–850 hPa temperature gradient, Denver sounding or mesoanalysis
variables.mechanism: Steep low-level lapse rates (near-dry-adiabatic) indicate superadiabatic mixing layer; combined with sufficient moisture, produces strong CAPE and potential for large hail.

variables.name: MeanRH
variables.label: Mean relative humidity
variables.source: Surface–500 hPa layer mean RH from sounding or model analysis
variables.mechanism: Layer-mean RH controls the size of CAPE and modulates hail melting below freezing level; VeryMoist environment supports large-hail growth and reduces melting.

variables.name: MidLLapse
variables.label: Mid-level lapse rate
variables.source: 700–500 hPa temperature gradient, Denver sounding
variables.mechanism: Steep mid-level lapse rates (EML signature) dramatically increase CAPE and hail-growth-layer depth; a 700–500 hPa lapse rate ≥8°C/km is a classic large-hail precursor for northeastern Colorado.

variables.name: MvmtFeatures
variables.label: Movement of synoptic features
variables.source: Short-range forecast/observed motion of fronts, upper troughs, jet streaks
variables.mechanism: Rapidly moving synoptic features import fresh forcing; StrongFront or MarkedUpper indicates dynamic lift that can overcome even strong capping.

variables.name: RHRatio
variables.label: Mid- to low-level RH ratio
variables.source: Ratio of mid-level to low-level RH
variables.mechanism: DryMMoistL (dry mid-levels over moist boundary layer) is the classic recipe for tall, efficient hail growth: high CAPE from steep lapse rates combined with dry air promoting large hailstones via reduced wet-bulb temperatures aloft.

variables.name: SfcWndShfDis
variables.label: Surface wind shifts and discontinuities
variables.source: Surface mesonet; radar fine-line and gust-front analysis
variables.mechanism: Surface boundaries (Denver Cyclone, dryline, frontal wind shifts) provide low-level convergence that is the most reliable convective trigger in northeastern Colorado; DenvCyclone is locally unique and strongly associated with supercell development.

variables.name: SynForcng
variables.label: Synoptic forcing tendency
variables.source: QG forcing / upper divergence / jet-streak analysis
variables.mechanism: Large-scale dynamic forcing (positive QG omega, jet-entrance divergence) that drives widespread ascent; SigPositive synoptic forcing can overcome substantial CIN and is necessary for widespread severe events.

variables.name: TempDis
variables.label: Temperature discontinuities
variables.source: Surface analysis / mesonet; frontal thermal boundaries
variables.mechanism: Thermal boundaries (fronts, outflow edges) create differential heating zones that enhance low-level wind shear and convective initiation along their leading edges.

variables.name: WindAloft
variables.label: Upper-level wind field
variables.source: 300–200 hPa wind analysis; jet stream position
variables.mechanism: Jet stream position determines upper-level divergence quadrant over the target area; NWQuad (downstream of trough) provides strongest divergence and ascent; SWQuad associated with anticyclonic shear and reduced storm-relative helicity.

variables.name: WindFieldMt
variables.label: Wind field over mountains
variables.source: 700 hPa analysis and mountain-station surface winds
variables.mechanism: Westerly flow enhances orographic lifting over the Front Range, promoting mountain storm development that can move onto the plains as severe-hail producers; light/variable flow reduces orographic initiation.

variables.name: WindFieldPln
variables.label: Wind field over plains
variables.source: Surface and 850 hPa wind analysis, northeastern Colorado plains
variables.mechanism: BL flow regime over the plains controls moisture transport, boundary-layer convergence, and storm motion. DenvCyclone and SEquad (southeasterly) flows are most strongly associated with severe hail via enhanced moisture flux and hodograph curvature.
